title: Dependencies with Parameters & Sub-dependencies
description: Pass arguments to dependencies and chain dependencies together.

slides.title: Parameterized Dependencies 🎛️
slides.content:
# Dependencies can have their own parameters

Just like path operations, dependencies can declare their own parameters (path, query, header, body, etc.).

FastAPI will resolve those parameters automatically, combining them with any parameters from the path operation.

This allows you to create highly reusable and configurable dependencies.

slides.title: Sub-dependencies: Dependencies that Depend on Others 🔗
slides.content:
# Chaining Dependencies

A dependency can itself depend on other dependencies. FastAPI will resolve the entire dependency tree.

Example:
- `get_current_user` depends on `get_token`.
- `get_current_user` is used in a path operation.

FastAPI will call `get_token` first, then pass its result to `get_current_user`.

quizData.question: In a chain of dependencies, which one runs first?

options.text: The dependency that is declared first in the code

quizData.explanation: FastAPI resolves the dependency tree from the leaves up. The most nested (sub-dependency) runs first, then its result is passed to the parent.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Sub-dependencies let you build modular, testable components. For example, you can have a database session dependency that depends on a configuration dependency.
